verdict: Caution — lend selectively to mid-size Bengaluru IT services and product firms with contracted, diversified revenue; avoid pure headcount-billing vendors exposed to AI-led pricing pressure and campus-hiring collapse.
title: Bengaluru Computer Software & IT: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A Bengaluru software firm sells skilled people and code, and gets paid weeks after the work is delivered.** Inputs are engineers, laptops and cloud capacity; output is billed time or a licensed product. Cash sits in receivables, not stock, so the working-capital cycle is the whole credit story — ICRA notes that a longer cycle means a larger funding requirement and a weaker liquidity profile [11]. **So when a proposal lands, check the receivable days and the top-customer share before you look at the P&L.**

## What has changed now
**The billable-hour model is being squeezed by AI, and campus hiring in Bengaluru has fallen** [1]. TCS still held margins while ramping AI investment, but its shares were down 30.3% year-to-date even after a 6.2% bounce [5]; AI is described as undermining the billable-hour model in a US$315-billion sector [5]. Against that, mid-caps are growing: Sasken revenue up 25.6% year-on-year to Rs. 321 crores with software services up 34% and EBITDA margin up 700 basis points [7], and InfoBeans grew 22% in constant currency while profit growth of 16% trailed revenue of 30%, with rising 90-day receivables [4]. **The split is real: large incumbents stall, focused mid-caps grow — but margin proof is not yet there** [4].

## Where the growth is
**Pursue mid-size firms (roughly the Sasken/InfoBeans shape) with a named product or embedded/engineering niche, not body-shop vendors.** Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026 (17–19 November) is pushing embedded systems, AI and robotics with 75+ countries participating [2][3] — that is where new order flow and partnerships will form. **Avoid vendors whose revenue is one client or one campus pipeline; the placement fall [1] hits their cost base and bench directly.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure as a receivables-backed working-capital line with a charge on book debts, not a clean term loan.** Take monthly: ageing of receivables beyond 90 days, top-five client concentration, and billed-versus-collected revenue. **If 90-day receivables rise while revenue grows, ask for the client-wise collection schedule** — that is the InfoBeans pattern [4]. Rating methodology flags US visa norms and geographic concentration as live risks for overseas-revenue firms [9]; collect from customer the US-revenue share and visa-dependent headcount.

## Early-warning signs
- **Bench strength rising while billing stays flat (monthly)** -> cut limit, ask for order book.
- **Any single client above 30% of revenue (quarterly)** -> require diversification covenant.
- **EBITDA margin falling while revenue grows (quarterly)** -> reprice or exit; this is the InfoBeans margin question [4].
- **Delay in statutory dues or salary (monthly)** -> stop fresh disbursal.
